title: Two frets: a whole step
summary: Leave one fret between the starting and ending positions.

steps.title: A bigger step
steps.body:
A **whole step**, also called a tone, is two half steps. On one string, move two frets to make a whole step. One fret lies between your starting and ending positions.

**Why it matters:** Whole steps and half steps are the small distances used to build longer patterns.

steps.title: A to B is two frets
steps.body: Open A to B at fret 2 on string 5 is a whole step. Compare it with B at fret 2 to C at fret 3: that move is only a half step.

items.prompt: Play A2, then go up a whole step. Use the lit positions.

steps.title: Compare one fret and two
steps.body: From the same starting fret, try one fret higher, then two frets higher. Say half step for one and whole step for two. Work slowly; speed is not the goal.

items.prompt: How far apart are these two notes?
Play A2 at fret 5 on string 6, then go down a whole step.
